reviewed: 2026-10-30 against production app_article 272 (draft), itineraries 2-4, FAQ, booking terms

ops.old:
Halong Bay vs Ninh Binh comes down to time. With one day from Hanoi, choose Ninh Binh: it is closer, you can get there by train, and its boats, bikes and temples fit into a day. With a night to spare, choose Ha Long Bay and sleep on the water. A Ha Long day trip spends about five hours on the road.

[IMAGE: Two-part view: limestone karsts rising from the sea in Ha Long Bay, and a small rowing boat on a river between rice fields and karst peaks in Ninh Binh | alt: Limestone karst scenery at sea in Ha Long Bay and among rivers and rice fields in Ninh Binh]

Halong Bay vs Ninh Binh: what is the real difference?

Both are limestone karst country. The difference is what surrounds the rock. In Ha Long Bay the towers rise out of the sea and you see them from a boat. In Ninh Binh they rise out of rivers and rice fields, which is why people call it "Ha Long Bay on land".

Both are UNESCO World Heritage sites, listed for different reasons. The Ha Long Bay and Cat Ba Archipelago World Heritage listing covers 65,650 hectares and 1,133 islands and islets, and UNESCO describes it as the most extensive and best-known example of marine-invaded tower karst. Since 2023 the listing has also covered the Cat Ba archipelago, which includes Lan Ha Bay. The Trang An Landscape Complex in Ninh Binh was inscribed in 2014 as a mixed cultural and natural site: karst peaks around partly submerged valleys, plus the Hoa Lu ancient capital and the Tam Coc and Bich Dong area.

Ha Long BayNinh Binh (Trang An, Tam Coc)
SettingSea, islands and isletsRivers, rice fields, caves and temples on land
How you see itCruise boat, kayak, bamboo boatRowing boat through caves, bicycle, on foot
Getting there from HanoiMost people go by road, about 2.5 hours to Tuan ChauTrain about 2h15, bus 2.5 to 3 hours, car around 2 hours depending on traffic
As a day tripPossible, but long for the time on the waterThe natural choice
Best withAt least one night on boardA full day, or a night if you want early starts
CrowdsBusy, with many vessels; Lan Ha Bay to the south is quieterTam Coc gets busy when day tours from Hanoi arrive

How long does it take to get there from Hanoi?

Ninh Binh is the easier journey. The railway line covers 115 km and the train takes about 2 hours 15 minutes, with around six departures a day according to Rough Guides. Timetables change by season, so check before you go. A bus takes 2.5 to 3 hours, and a car or van around 2 hours depending on traffic. Many vans drop you in Tam Coc or at Trang An, so you are on a boat soon after you arrive.

For Ha Long Bay, almost everyone goes by road: about 2.5 hours to Tuan Chau, where most cruises check in. The drive times are closer than people expect. What matters is what those hours buy you once you arrive.

Is Ninh Binh or Halong Bay better as a day trip from Hanoi?

Ninh Binh, clearly. The sights sit close together: the Trang An boat wharf is a short drive west of central Ninh Binh, with Hoa Lu to the north and Tam Coc and Bich Dong to the south. A typical day is a rowing-boat trip through the caves at Trang An or Tam Coc, then a bike ride along the paddies and a stop at the Hoa Lu temples. You set your own pace, and if the train suits you, you never sit in a van at all.

Two honest caveats. Boat routes, ticket prices and opening hours at Trang An change, and published figures disagree, so check locally on the day rather than relying on old numbers. And Tam Coc gets crowded once the day-tour buses from Hanoi arrive. If you want the river quieter, start early or stay a night in Ninh Binh.

A Ha Long day trip is possible, and plenty of people do it. The maths is the problem: around five hours in a vehicle for a few hours on the water, and you leave before evening, so you never see the bay at sunset or first light. If a day is all you have, Ninh Binh gives you more for it.

[IMAGE: Rowing boat with passengers entering a low limestone cave on the river at Trang An, rice fields and karst peaks behind | alt: Rowing boat entering a cave on the river at Trang An, Ninh Binh]

Why does Ha Long Bay work better with a night on board?

The road time stays the same whether you stay one night or none. What changes is everything after boarding: an afternoon among the islands, the evening at anchor, and an early morning on deck before you head back. That is the part of Ha Long that day visitors miss.

Be realistic about the downsides. Ha Long is the famous bay and it is busy, with many vessels on the water. Cruise programmes run to fixed times, which some travellers find regimented. After a full day the karst can start to look alike, which is one reason a single night suits most first-time visitors. If calm matters more than the classic views, Lan Ha Bay, just south near Cat Ba Island, has the same limestone scenery with far fewer boats.

What a two-day Ha Long cruise looks like

We operate Green Ruby Cruises, so treat this as an example of the format rather than an independent recommendation. Our Ha Long Bay 2 days 1 night itinerary on Green Ruby 1 runs like this:

  • 10:45: check-in at the Green Ruby lounge at Tuan Chau (pick-up in Hanoi is at 08:00 if you arrange a transfer).
  • 11:45: tender boat to the ship, then safety briefing, cabins and lunch on board.
  • 15:30: Luon Cave by kayak or bamboo boat.
  • 16:30: Ti Top Island: climb to the summit for the view, or swim.
  • Evening: sunset on deck, dinner, a cooking class and squid fishing after dark.
  • Day 2, 06:15: morning on deck and breakfast; 08:00 Sung Sot Cave; 09:30 brunch as the ship returns to port.

Green Ruby runs overnight cruises only, no day trips. The ships are not in service yet: both are expected to start sailing in February 2027, a provisional date. Our brand facts page sets out the current status. We do not publish prices yet; the reservations team handles quotes.

[IMAGE: Kayaks paddling through the arch at Luon Cave into the enclosed lagoon, Ha Long Bay | alt: Kayakers passing through Luon Cave in Ha Long Bay]

When is the best time to visit each?

Both places share northern Vietnam's climate, so the same calendar broadly works for both.

  • October to April: cool and dry, and the most popular season. October to November and March to April are the most comfortable months on the water. Winter evenings on deck are cool, so pack a warm layer. In Ninh Binh, winter days can be grey and drizzly.
  • May to September: warm, and the best months for swimming in the bay. It is also storm season, so cruise itineraries can change for safety, sometimes at short notice.

Ninh Binh has one seasonal draw Ha Long lacks: the rice harvest. The paddies along the Ngo Dong River at Tam Coc turn gold in early summer, as this VnExpress photo report shows. Local guides put the harvests at roughly late May to early June and again around September to October, with the gold lasting only two to three weeks. Treat those dates as approximate and ask locally if you are planning around them.

Can you do both Ha Long Bay and Ninh Binh in one trip?

Yes, and with three or more days outside Hanoi it is the plan we would suggest. Use Hanoi as the hinge: Ninh Binh as a day trip on one day, then a two-day Ha Long cruise. On a one-night cruise, brunch is served from 09:30 as the ship heads back to port, which leaves the afternoon for the drive back.

With four or five days, stay a night in Ninh Binh to get on the river early, and give Ha Long two nights. On a three-day cruise such as the Halong Immersion, 3 days 2 nights, the middle day goes by day boat to Cua Van floating village, Tien Ong Cave and a pearl farm, quieter corners that one night does not reach. If you are flying out after the cruise, Cat Bi International Airport in Hai Phong is about 45 minutes to an hour from the port.

[IMAGE: Early morning on a cruise sundeck in Ha Long Bay, mist between the karst islands | alt: Early morning view of karst islands from a cruise deck in Ha Long Bay]

Frequently asked questions

Will I get seasick on Ha Long Bay?

Rarely. The water is sheltered by the islands and usually calm. If you are sensitive to motion, bring a remedy as a precaution.

What happens if bad weather stops the cruise?

Local authorities can restrict sailing in bad weather, most often in the May to September storm season. On Green Ruby, guests in that situation may receive a full refund, a new date or a replacement service, depending on the circumstances.

Should I choose Lan Ha Bay instead of Ha Long Bay?

If quiet matters more than the famous views, yes. On the two-day Lan Ha Bay cruise you still check in at Tuan Chau, then a tender takes you to Gia Luan Pier to board, with kayaking at Ao Ech Lagoon on the second morning.

Do I need my passport for an overnight cruise?

Yes. Bring your passport along with swimwear and sunscreen; it is on the packing list for every Green Ruby itinerary.

How do I plan the cruise part of the trip?

If you have settled the Halong Bay vs Ninh Binh choice with a day in Ninh Binh and a night on the water, the reservations team can answer questions about dates, cabins and Hanoi transfers through our contact page.

Will I get seasick on Ha Long Bay?

Local authorities can restrict sailing in bad weather, most often in the May to September storm season. Under Green Ruby's booking terms, if the authorities restrict navigation before departure, you will be offered a new departure date or a full refund of the affected cruise booking. If a cruise that has already begun has to be shortened, the company will make a fair adjustment based on the services provided.
